question.prompt: The PRD defines the holdings and overlay behavior but does not provide the web URL or stable authenticated entry point for the dashboard page that contains the Top Holdings card. What should these web tests start from?

options.label: Use placeholder
options.detail: Author and parameterize the suite with {{dashboard_url}} as the starting URL for the dashboard page that contains the Top Holdings card.

options.label: Add source
options.detail: Provide a source or exact URL that states the stable dashboard entry point for this page.

content.risk_rationale: All eight tests are web flows and each one requires a concrete starting URL; the suite can be authored with {{dashboard_url}}, but execution is blocked until an environment-specific entry point is supplied.

content.title: Open the in-page security modal from the preview
content.test_md_blob:
# Open the in-page security modal from the preview

> Prove OPEN SECURITY in the preview opens the in-page modal and the modal shows the required security detail sections.

## Step 1

Open {{dashboard_url}} and wait until the dashboard page with the Top Holdings card is fully visible.

## Step 2

Capture baseline: no security modal is open on the dashboard.

## Step 3

In the Top Holdings card, explicitly activate the NVDA ticker to open its security preview popover.

## Step 4

From the NVDA security preview popover, activate OPEN SECURITY.

## Step 5

Assert that an in-page security modal is now visible and that it shows security name, ticker, price, daily move, chart, fundamentals, analyst consensus, and recent news.

## Step 6 — assert @verifies ac-61, ac-62

Confirm state-transition check: security modal open (equals) — the stated promise: Activating OPEN SECURITY from the preview opens an in-page security modal.
content.objectives_blob:

  - objective: Open {{dashboard_url}} and wait until the dashboard page with the Top Holdings card is fully visible.
    step: 1
  - baseline: true
    objective: 'Capture baseline: no security modal is open on the dashboard.'
    step: 2
  - objective: In the Top Holdings card, explicitly activate the NVDA ticker to open its security preview popover.
    step: 3
  - objective: From the NVDA security preview popover, activate OPEN SECURITY.
    step: 4
  - objective: Assert that an in-page security modal is now visible and that it shows security name, ticker, price, daily move, chart, fundamentals, analyst consensus, and recent news.
    step: 5
  - check:
      baseline: security modal closed
      expected_mode: authored
      kind: state-transition
      operand: security modal open
      operator: equals
      review_required: false
      verified_against: ac-61
    objective: 'Confirm state-transition check: security modal open (equals) — the stated promise: Activating OPEN SECURITY from the preview opens an in-page security modal.'
    step: 6

Store the Top Holdings card width and the NVDA row height as baseline_layout before any preview is open.

## Step 2

## Step 3

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Scored highest because this path is the bridge from lightweight preview to full security inspection, and a failure here breaks the deeper drill-in flow entirely.

[value_score] Scored next because explicit ticker activation is one of the two named preview-entry methods and also covers the no-reflow plus preview-content promises on a deliberate interaction path.
[value_score] Scored just below explicit activation because hover is the second named preview-entry method and can regress independently in pointer-driven behavior.
[value_score] Scored high because Escape is a keyboard dismissal route with accessibility implications; if it fails, keyboard users can become trapped in the modal.
[value_score] Scored high because the close button is the primary visible dismissal affordance and must work even if shortcut handling regresses.
[value_score] Scored high because backdrop-click dismissal is a distinct overlay behavior that commonly regresses separately from button-based closing.
[value_score] Scored high because this negative path guards against accidental dismissal while a user is interacting with modal content.

[value_score] Scored lowest of the kept set because it confirms default holdings content and columns, but failures there are more presentation-oriented than the overlay-chain interaction failures above.

[self_critique] Oracle proof check: each modal open or close test captured the required baseline state before the action, and the preview plus holdings tests asserted directly observable on-screen results instead of inferring success from indirect signals.

[self_critique] Technique fit check: the suite kept hover and explicit activation separate, and it split each close route into its own scenario-test pair because the PRD names those interactions independently and their outcomes can diverge.

[self_critique] Negative coverage check: the suite included sc-25 as the required must-not-close interaction because that is the only explicit negative behavior the source states for this use-case; no additional negative family was evidenced in the PRD lines used here.

[self_critique] Assert breadth check: I did not widen assertions to modal dimensions, backdrop color, popover elevation, or animation timing because those details were not part of the committed acceptance criteria for this run and would have over-broadened the tests.
